citations.quote: Study A6181004 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, international Phase 3 clinical trial in 56 centers on three continents.

The major clinical study supporting the safety and efficacy of sunitinib was Study A6181004, a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of sunitinib versus placebo in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who were intolerant of or who had disease progression during prior imatinib treatment.

population.text: Patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who were intolerant of or who had disease progression during prior imatinib treatment

citations.quote: The major clinical study supporting the safety and efficacy of sunitinib was Study A6181004, a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of sunitinib versus placebo in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) who were intolerant of or who had disease progression during prior imatinib treatment.

endpoint.text: Time to tumor progression (TTP), time from randomization to first documentation of objective tumor progression

citations.quote: The primary objective of Study A6181004 was to compare the time to tumor progression (TTP) in patients receiving sunitinib plus best supportive care to patients receiving placebo plus best supportive care.
Time to Tumor Progression (TTP) was defined as the time from randomization to first documentation of objective tumor progression.
The intent-to-treat (ITT) population included 312 patients. Two-hundred seven patients were randomized to the SUTENT arm, and 105 patients were randomized to the placebo arm.

result.text: At planned interim analysis after 149 TTP events, median TTP 27.3 weeks (SUTENT) vs 6.4 weeks (placebo), HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.23, 0.47), p<0.0001

citations.quote: After 149 progression events had occurred, an interim analysis for efficacy revealed that patients on SUTENT experienced a more than four-fold increase in median TTP from 6.4 to 27.3 weeks (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.23-0.47, log-rank P < 0.0001).

indication.text: SUTENT is indicated for the treatment of gastrointestinal stromal tumor after disease progression on or intolerance to imatinib mesylate.

citations.quote: SUTENT is indicated for the treatment of gastrointestinal stromal tumor after disease progression on or intolerance to imatinib mesylate.

target_moa.text: Small-molecule oral multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor that blocks signaling via multiple RTKs including VEGFR, PDGFR, KIT and FLT-3

citations.quote: SUTENT is a small-molecule inhibitor of receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs).

Sunitinib (SU011248, Sutent) is a small molecule, receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) inhibitor that blocks signaling via multiple RTKs including vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF), KIT and FLT-3.
SUTENT is a small-molecule inhibitor of receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs).

key_safety.text: In GIST Study A, Grade 3/4 treatment-emergent AEs occurred in 56% (SUTENT) vs 51% (placebo). Common AEs (SUTENT vs placebo) included fatigue (42% vs 47%), diarrhea (40% vs 27%), nausea (31% vs 32%), and mucositis/stomatitis (29% vs 18%); decreased LVEF was increased on SUTENT (11%) vs placebo (3%)
